source.publication: 2025 MI-1040 Forms and Instructions (includes Form 4884 instructions)
source.section: Schedule 1 line 28 and its worksheet lines 1-8 (PDF page 17: maximum 29,376 joint, reduced by line 27 retirement benefits); Form 4884 Section A (PDF page 20 'Recipients born before 1946'); PDF page 3; MI-1040 lines 9a, 10, 13-17 (PDF page 10 Line 9a, Line 10, Line 17; PDF page 11 example: line 14 income subject to tax less line 15 exemptions = line 16 taxable income)

worked: Federal AGI = spouse 1 private pension 5,000.00 + interest 40,000.00 + dividends 10,000.00 + long-term gains 5,000.00 + taxable Social Security 34,000.00 = 94,000.00. Federal taxable income = 94,000.00 - federal standard deduction (31,500 + 2 x 1,600 age 65 or older = 34,700.00) = 59,300.00; given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored. Michigan (older spouse born 1938): Schedule 1 line 14 Social Security 34,000.00. Section A: private pension 5,000.00, under the 131,794.00 limit, all on line 27 (this tests pre1946_private below its cap). Line 28 worksheet: line 1 29,376.00; line 2 0.00; line 3 5,000.00; line 4 0.00; line 5 5,000.00; line 6 = 24,376.00; line 7 interest, dividends and gains 40,000.00 + 10,000.00 + 5,000.00 = 55,000.00; line 8 smaller 24,376.00 (the reduced cap binds). Subtractions 34,000.00 + 5,000.00 + 24,376.00 = 63,376.00. Line 14 = 94,000.00 - 63,376.00 = 30,624.00; exemptions 11,600.00; line 16 = 19,024.00. MI-1040 line 17 tax = 19,024.00 x 0.0425 = 808.52. No credits; state income tax 808.52.
